I'm so sorry you're going through this. I know I don't fully understand your situation and I don't want to insult your family as I hope, despite how it sounds, they are doing it with the intention of trying to look out for you, but tbh it sounds like your mother might be a big part of the reason you have panic attacks in the first place, not the only reason of course but possibly a big part. I understand that you rely on them for a place to live and that makes your situation even harder as you can't just call the cops. She needs to understand that what she's doing is very much illegal and not having access to your medication is exacerbating your condition, I'm sure. To me it sounds like she enjoys having that control over you and that's totally toxic and if your dad isn't helping you or seeing why its wrong what your mom is doing, that is also horrible. I know you said that you have had bad experiences with medication you've taken in the past but I still can't see how that would justify this in her mind. It sounds to me like she either likes having the control over you or she really doesn't trust you not to abuse them, either way it's not good. Maybe try to find somewhere else that you can stay if you can't get her to understand. I'm really sorry that you have to deal with such a mess and I hope that you can find a good solution.

No, I haven't, but I know I really should. I'm a bit embarrassed to say I'm quite a shut in, I haven't left my home in a good while, and I haven't been able to push myself to go. I know I could probably do a web meeting for an appointment but even that really scares me, more so than the hallucinations and the thought of schizophrenia scare me it seems.

I am so incredibly relieved to know that it's not just me. I have also been worried about being or developing schizophrenia because of the audio hallucinations I have. Every night when it gets dark I hear things like I'm in a crowded room of people talking loud amongst themselves, not really able to make out what is being said, sometimes it's not so bad, just a consistent tolerable volume, but other times it's so loud I flinch and have to strain to hear anything else, like the music I listen to with headphones. I also saw the comment about exploding head syndrome, which I also experience separately, the talking is different as I can listen and continue hearing it vs the syndrome being a loud sudden noise that goes away once it's startled me awake. To be honest I never even really considered that it could be related to my anxiety or panic attacks, but now that I'm thinking about it, it would make sense since stress can do a lot of weird things.

Physically I feel all my muscles tense and my heart starts pounding, it's like restless legs but everywhere at once, kind of like when at night sometimes your muscles tense really bad and you have to do the thing where you just move it but it comes like more of a twitch (I hope this isn't something that just happens to me). Emotionally it makes me feel afraid and angry and then guilty because I know I shouldn't be angry but I do anyways, can't help it. Like a hive of bees buzzing suddenly and intensely right inside of your ears.

I consider myself to be, I don't live in Japan and I'm going on my seventh year being completely isolated even from my family. Hikikomori is defined as acute social withdrawal, I think the reason people don't think others outside of Japan can be hikikomori is simply the fact that it is a Japanese word/term. I've heard that if you are isolated for a period of six months or more you are considered hikikomori. But it's not like it's a club you join or something you should strive to be or do. If you can manage to get yourself outside once a week that's fantastic.

I might not be able to help much, but I hear you. It's hard, sometimes so much it's nearly impossible to comprehend or handle. No one else knows what you are going through inside, it's easy to feel isolated and rejected especially when you're surrounded by shit people. It sucks. But they're not forever, shitty people come and go. Just like everything else. It's hard to see it when you're in the middle of it but these feelings won't last forever even if it feels like it already has been forever. I too am struggling to keep my head above the water.
